item.title: Follow the community fridge policy
item.summary: A volunteer gives a new helper the reasoning behind collection and labelling rules.
item.transcript_text:
Volunteer: Most people think the community fridge is only for food that shops would throw away. Local residents can donate too, but we handle the two kinds of donations differently.
Helper: Is that why there are two boxes of labels?
Volunteer: Yes. Shops tell us when their items came off the shelf, so their label has a date and the shop name. At home, anyone can open a packet, so residents can only give sealed items. Put those on the top shelf and write down the date we received them.
Helper: Someone offered us homemade soup yesterday.
Volunteer: We cannot take it here. Ask them whether the café wants it for a shared lunch. The café can talk to them about how they made it.

questions.prompt: What does the volunteer mainly explain?
options: Why a fridge should stand beside a café
How people can apply for food vouchers
How to handle two sources of donated food
Which shops sell the cheapest food
questions.explanation: The conversation contrasts the procedures for shops and residents.

questions.prompt: Why can residents donate only sealed items?
options: The team cannot check what happened after opening
The shop labels will not stick to open items
The top shelf is reserved for cold packages
Residents can give food only once
questions.explanation: The volunteer says a packet may have been opened at home.

questions.prompt: What belongs on the top shelf?
options: Every donation from a shop
Homemade soup in any pot
Only food with no date
Qualifying items donated by residents
questions.explanation: The volunteer directs eligible resident donations to the top shelf.

questions.prompt: What should happen to the offer of soup?
options: Put the soup in the fridge anyway
Report the donor to the shop
Ask the donor to check with the café
Put a shop label on the container
questions.explanation: The fridge cannot take it, but the donor can ask the café about its rules.
